items.title: Observe instability during unattended runs
items.takeaway: Track retries and completion in unattended runs, and keep a separate record of the supervising model.
items.observation: The tester reports launch-day instability when running Neon headlessly and says Opus 5.5 monitored the run.
items.body_notes: The screenshots document that environment. The report does not attribute the root cause.

items.title: Build a simulated logic-gate demo
items.takeaway: Check what the simulation shows at the chip, circuit board and display levels.
items.observation: The author shows an interactive electronics demo that goes from simulated logic gates and circuit boards to a retro terminal display.
items.body_notes: The series reports one prompt per demo without refinement. The recording shows the interface and simulation behavior.

items.title: Design a Bluetooth toothbrush in tscircuit
items.takeaway: Review routing and footprint selection independently of the rendered enclosure.
items.observation: A tscircuit maintainer compared Neon High, Opus 5.5 High and Sol 6.2 High on a Bluetooth electric toothbrush.
items.body_notes: The maintainer preferred Neon's visual result but reported incomplete routing and poor footprint choices.

items.title: Relay a Muse side conversation to Neon
items.takeaway: Check which replies come from Neon before relying on the Muse relay.
items.observation: The author built a Muse side chat that passes requests and replies through to Neon.
items.body_notes: The posted Japanese instruction configures the Muse relay. It is an instruction to Muse and does not establish a direct prompt sent to Neon.

items.title: Use Neon for copy in a three-model T3 Code workflow
items.takeaway: Assign one model to copywriting and check its handoff to implementation and playtesting.
items.observation: The developer gives Neon the copywriting role within a multi-model T3 Code workflow.
items.body_notes: The developer assigns implementation to Fable and playtesting to GPT-6.2 Astra. The T3 Code screenshot shows a creature-raising game with copywriters in the active workflow.

items.title: Rework a Spotify recommendation MCP
items.takeaway: Review recommendation changes and test whether unrequested features improve the result.
items.observation: The creator used Neon to revise a Spotify recommendation MCP originally built with Argon.
items.body_notes: The creator reported bug fixes and an unrequested taste-based recommendation model. The post does not provide recommendation accuracy.

items.title: Draw an SVG side view of a car
items.takeaway: Check proportion and silhouette when comparing code-rendered side views.
items.observation: The creator used Neon high in AI Studio to create a BMW M4 CS side-view SVG.
items.body_notes: The artifact is attached to the post. No complete prompt is quoted.

items.title: Run an SVG test series
items.takeaway: Review several outputs before judging consistency across SVG tasks.
items.observation: The tester shared three outputs in a Neon SVG test series.
items.body_notes: The results are presented together and counted as one test series.

items.title: Animate a pelican in Three.js
items.takeaway: Check the cycling motion and scene rendering as separate parts of the animation.
items.observation: The tester attributes a Three.js pelican-on-a-bicycle output to Neon.
items.body_notes: The creator provides a recording but no timing or reasoning setting.

items.title: Draw an SVG portrait at xhigh
items.takeaway: Assess likeness and SVG editability separately in a portrait test.
items.observation: The tester shares a portrait of Ana de Armas attributed to Neon xhigh.
items.body_notes: The source gives the subject and effort setting without the exact prompt.

items.title: Animate a cycling pelican at medium effort
items.takeaway: Use a fixed animation task to compare results at different reasoning settings.
items.observation: The author used Neon at medium effort to produce a pelican cycling demo and posted the video.
items.body_notes: The clip documents this creator's separate run of a common test task.

items.title: Compare two voxel garden scenes
items.takeaway: Check similar-looking outputs against total run cost and the settings each source discloses.
items.observation: The author posted a voxel garden from Neon xhigh alongside a GPT-6.2 Sol xhigh result.
items.body_notes: The source identifies the first image as Neon and reports USD 1.01 versus USD 0.19 for Sol. The post does not specify whether the prompts and tools matched.

items.title: Generate a Three.js and GLSL scene
items.takeaway: Separate shader behavior, scene geometry, and generation time in a graphics test.
items.observation: The creator shares a Three.js and GLSL output from Neon and reports a run of two minutes and 40 seconds.
items.body_notes: The main post points to the replies for the instruction without quoting it.

items.title: Create paintings entirely in code
items.takeaway: Open the rendered examples to see how code can produce a coherent visual series.
items.observation: The creator reports using early-access Neon to write code that renders paintings.
items.body_notes: The source provides a set of results from the same series. It does not supply each exact prompt.

items.title: Compare pelican cycling animations
items.takeaway: Compare the reported runtime with the movement and scene details in the same video.
items.observation: The tester compared a pelican animation across Neon, Hydrogen, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol.
items.body_notes: The author reports a three-minute Neon run and preferred its appearance. The recorded Sol-only follow-up belongs to the same test.

items.title: Compare Three.js cycling animations across three models
items.takeaway: Use the labeled clips to compare motion, lighting, and scene composition.
items.observation: The tester published a Three.js cycling comparison of Neon, Opus 5.5 and Carbon.
items.body_notes: The author preferred Neon over Opus and judged it close to Carbon. This is the author's visual assessment.

items.title: Render a tall ship on the ocean
items.takeaway: Inspect whether wave animation and ship rendering remain coherent throughout the clip.
items.observation: The tester shared an ocean sailing scene attributed to Neon xhigh.
items.body_notes: The video shows an animated sailing ship. The source does not supply a specific workflow or timing.

items.title: Generate a voxel pagoda
items.takeaway: Use the voxel scene to assess layering, silhouette, and composition.
items.observation: The tester posts a voxel pagoda generated at Neon xhigh.
items.body_notes: The post includes the rendered result and the author's design reaction.

items.title: Draw a frustrated pelican on a bicycle
items.takeaway: Check whether the character expression and bicycle motion both read clearly.
items.observation: The creator used Neon high in AI Studio to draw an SVG of a frustrated pelican riding a bicycle.
items.body_notes: The post shows the result and identifies the effort setting.

items.title: Compare gamepad drawings with GPT-6.2 Sol
items.takeaway: Compare render quality and time and cost separately for the two gamepad outputs.
items.observation: The tester used the same prompt at each model's highest available reasoning and judged the outputs similar.
items.body_notes: The author reported 20 minutes and about USD 1.60 for Neon versus nine minutes and about USD 0.53 for Sol.

items.title: Generate a 3D seaplane
items.takeaway: Review the seaplane and water interaction before judging the prototype as a whole.
items.observation: The tester used Neon xhigh to build a 3D seaplane and shared a video.
items.body_notes: The creator describes the build as fast and the interface as cleaner, without giving a wall-clock measurement.

items.title: Draw a 2D horse
items.takeaway: Treat the horse clip as a visual example and keep cross-model settings in mind.
items.observation: The creator used Neon to produce a two-dimensional horse and posted the output.
items.body_notes: The creator preferred it to their prior Gemini results. The post does not provide matching settings.

items.title: Test a rainy convenience-store scene
items.takeaway: Use the matched scene to assess how presentation changes with shorter generation time.
items.observation: The tester used the same prompt for Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol and posted the comparison.
items.body_notes: The author preferred the Sol visual output while reporting faster, cheaper completion for Neon in this run.

items.title: Animate a robotic quadruped from one image
items.takeaway: Check gait and movement separately from how closely the scene follows the reference.
items.observation: The developer gave Neon a single reference image and asked for a 3D model.
items.body_notes: The developer reports a Three.js WebGPU demonstration with four-leg inverse kinematics and walk, trot and gallop animations.

items.title: Animate Keats in vanilla JavaScript
items.takeaway: Compare animation and brushwork when using code to interpret a literary source.
items.observation: A Google team member credits GeokenAI and Neon for a vanilla JavaScript animation of Keats's To Autumn.
items.body_notes: The post describes a 12 fps painterly 3D animation with no libraries. The sharing account is distinct from the credited creator.

items.title: Create a Triceratops demo
items.takeaway: Inspect the reconstruction sequence as well as the final visual.
items.observation: The creator attributes the Triceratops demonstration to Neon.
items.body_notes: The video shows the artifact. The post does not specify the input format or generation steps.

items.title: Compare 3D gear train renderings
items.takeaway: Use the labeled settings and output geometry to compare all four gear-train renders.
items.observation: The tester shows gear mechanism renders for Neon, Carbon, Astra and Sol across the labeled reasoning levels.
items.body_notes: The author favored Neon. The clip documents one visual comparison and does not establish the general cost claim.

items.title: Build ten interactive effects in a single HTML file
items.takeaway: Check whether the effects stay responsive and readable within a small HTML payload.
items.observation: A Google team member reports using Neon to create ten interactive 3D effects in one 27 KB HTML file.
items.body_notes: The demo includes shaders, water and lighting. The variations are grouped as one published project.

items.title: Build a Blender lab bench with Antigravity Swarm
items.takeaway: Trace which work Swarm coordinates and which operations Blender performs.
items.observation: Google demonstrated Neon using Antigravity Swarm and Blender to produce a lab-bench scene themed around the Gemini 4 family.
items.body_notes: The clip is a provider demo of the integrated workflow.

items.title: Compare architectural illustrations with Opus 5.5
items.takeaway: Set the same visual task and compare the output quality, run time, and cost independently.
items.observation: The tester compared the models using the same prompt at their highest available reasoning.
items.body_notes: The author reported about 20 minutes and USD 3.50 for Neon and 18 minutes and USD 7.20 for Opus, preferring the Opus output.

items.title: Visualize Voyager 1's flight
items.takeaway: Review the transitions between the launch, flyby and close-up when judging the sequence.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D Voyager 1 sequence that moves from launch to a Jupiter encounter and a close-up of the spacecraft.
items.body_notes: The author describes this as one unrefined prompt in the series. No trajectory validation is reported.

items.title: Build a 3D planetarium
items.takeaway: Check whether the planet and constellation views work together as a simple educational demo.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D planetarium moving between planets and a constellation view.
items.body_notes: The recording shows examples including Earth and Saturn. The one-prompt series does not establish astronomical precision.

items.title: Visualize Babbage's Difference Engine No. 2
items.takeaway: Look at the gear motion, numerical display and full-machine view when reviewing the visualization.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D visualization of Babbage's Difference Engine No. 2 with its gear assemblies and a numerical display.
items.body_notes: The recording moves between close-ups of the moving mechanism and a view of the complete machine.

items.title: Visualize the Antikythera mechanism
items.takeaway: Compare the recovered fragment view, gear reconstruction and dial readout in the same demo.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D Antikythera mechanism demo that switches between the recovered object, reconstructed gears and a dial.
items.body_notes: The recording shows a display of the assembly and details of the moving mechanism.

items.title: Prototype a visual wind tunnel
items.takeaway: Compare how the streamlines change between test shapes before using the visualization as a teaching example.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D wind-tunnel demo with visible airflow streamlines around different shapes.
items.body_notes: The video includes an aircraft and other test shapes. It gives no independent accuracy check for the simulation.

items.title: Create a King's College Chapel cutaway
items.takeaway: Compare the exterior, nave and cutaway to see how each view explains the building.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D cutaway of King's College Chapel that switches between the exterior and interior.
items.body_notes: The scene uses different views to show the nave, windows and the building's cross-section.

items.title: Render a river viaduct and its surroundings
items.takeaway: Use the near, far and wireframe views to assess both the bridge and its surrounding scene.
items.observation: The author shows a 3D river valley with a multi-arch viaduct, a train and several render views.
items.body_notes: The recording switches between near and distant camera angles and includes a wireframe-like view.

items.title: Build a Cambridge-inspired 3D city view
items.takeaway: Check how landmarks and the river remain recognizable as the camera moves through the scene.
items.observation: The author shows a city visualization inspired by Cambridge, with aerial and closer views of the modeled blocks.
items.body_notes: The clip shows the river, buildings and scene overlays. The author describes the setting as Cambridge-like.

items.title: Render a neon-themed Earth
items.takeaway: Check whether the visual theme is consistent as the globe rotates.
items.observation: The creator used Neon high in Antigravity to render a neon-themed planet.
items.body_notes: The source provides the result and effort setting.

items.title: Iterate a yacht scene
items.takeaway: Review before-and-after artifacts when asking the model to refine a 3D scene.
items.observation: The creator reports that Neon improved a yacht scene and shows the output.
items.body_notes: Firebase deployment was a stated intention at the time of the post.

items.title: Make costume materials in a custom VFX tool
items.takeaway: Compare treatments of the same costume form when choosing a material.
items.observation: The creator used Neon to make costume materials and posted six images of results.
items.body_notes: The creator describes the VFX tooling as their own. The source does not establish an independent performance comparison.

items.title: Compare voxel Ninjago scenes
items.takeaway: Judge visual framing and cost separately in a same-subject voxel comparison.
items.observation: The source compares Neon and Fable 5.2 on a voxel recreation.
items.body_notes: The author reports USD 12.93 for Neon and USD 11.19 for Fable and preferred the latter's framing.

items.title: Create a pelican product motion graphic
items.takeaway: Look at timing and typography together in a short product animation.
items.observation: The creator credits Neon with a pelican-themed product motion graphic.
items.body_notes: The linked clip shows the output. The post does not describe implementation or an exact prompt.

items.title: Compare New York City scene prototypes
items.takeaway: Evaluate landmark fidelity and runtime performance separately in a city-scene build.
items.observation: The tester reports that Neon included the Brooklyn Bridge, Statue of Liberty and a street with taxis.
items.body_notes: The tester preferred some details in the Opus output and reported that running the Neon scene lagged their PC.

items.title: Run a banana visual test
items.takeaway: Inspect how a simple visual task holds up across details and proportions.
items.observation: The tester posts a Neon output for a test titled Banana Test.
items.body_notes: The output is attached to the source. The source does not provide an exact prompt.

items.title: Compare a haunted cathedral on one prompt
items.takeaway: Use the published prompt to compare the two cathedral renders under the conditions described.
items.observation: The tester gave Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol the same haunted cathedral task.
items.body_notes: The creator reports USD 2.67 for Neon and USD 1.69 for Sol, with no clear visual winner in their assessment.
items.prompt_text: Build a huge haunted vampire cathedral

items.title: Prototype a phone assembly in Antigravity
items.takeaway: Check component fidelity and final assembly separately when reviewing a design prototype.
items.observation: The developer used Neon in Antigravity and showed a board of design components and a rendered phone assembly.
items.body_notes: The developer reports early impressions of coding and speed, without timings or a controlled Carbon comparison.

items.title: Generate an interactive historical sailing ship
items.takeaway: Inspect the boundaries between the ship and water in the interactive output.
items.observation: The author posted a zero-shot 3D sailing ship demonstration.
items.body_notes: The author reports that the ship and water rendered in distinct layers and describes the output as more realistic than their Sol result.

items.title: Design a model introduction in JavaScript
items.takeaway: Review typography and pacing in the JavaScript motion graphic.
items.observation: The author used Neon to make a motion graphic introducing the model.
items.body_notes: The author says it uses JavaScript without external assets.

items.title: Generate a ski hut scene in one pass
items.takeaway: Check the hut, snow, and trees separately when assessing this one-pass scene comparison.
items.observation: DesignArena asked Neon and Argon to generate the same Alpine hut setting and published the side-by-side outputs.
items.body_notes: DesignArena preferred elements of both renderings. It reports that Neon added snowfall without being asked.

items.title: Render a voxel fantasy castle
items.takeaway: Review the final scene and the reported run time when evaluating a one-prompt build.
items.observation: The creator shares a voxel castle produced at Neon xhigh.
items.body_notes: The creator reports one prompt and a 27-minute completion time.

items.title: Compare an octopus cycling animation with Astra
items.takeaway: Compare the animation and cost while keeping the two reasoning settings explicit.
items.observation: The tester recorded Astra xhigh at 21 minutes 53 seconds and USD 2.52, and Neon high at 41 minutes and USD 4.02.
items.body_notes: The author calls the animation quality close. This is one run at different reasoning settings.

items.title: Three.js butterfly animation
items.takeaway: Use the clip and its reported resource use to size a similar Three.js experiment.
items.observation: A creator used Neon xhigh in Antigravity to build a Three.js butterfly animation.
items.body_notes: The creator reported 57 minutes, about 23% of their five-hour quota, and 7% of their weekly quota.

items.title: Build components and motion from reference images
items.takeaway: Supply visual references and evaluate layout fidelity and motion as separate criteria.
items.observation: The creator used visual references to generate several components and accompanying motion.
items.body_notes: The demo shows the result. The claim about how it feels compared with Opus is the creator's judgment.

items.title: Pixel wizard world in Three.js
items.takeaway: Use the three passes to judge how visual polish changes with iteration.
items.observation: A creator gave Neon reference images and refined the Three.js scene over three passes.
items.body_notes: The creator reported using 39% of their five-hour quota and 11% of their weekly quota in Antigravity.

items.title: Castle rendering benchmark
items.takeaway: Treat the castle as one creator's visual benchmark and retain account-specific quota context.
items.observation: The creator used Neon for a castle benchmark and posted video and stills.
items.body_notes: The creator reported using about 4% of a weekly quota on their plan. The post does not establish whether that usage generalizes to other accounts.

items.title: Recreate Alan Turing's 1936 study
items.takeaway: Check archival fidelity and interactive functionality as separate parts of the reconstruction.
items.observation: Google used Neon with Antigravity Swarm to build an interactive reconstruction from archival photos.
items.body_notes: The scene includes King's Chapel, Turing's study and a working simulation of a universal Turing machine on the desk.

items.title: Build a side-scrolling obstacle game
items.takeaway: Test the obstacle loop and collision behavior when you review a small game prototype.
items.observation: The tester asked Neon for a Flappy Bird-style prototype and posted a recording.
items.body_notes: The author reports about five minutes and discusses their own impressions of cost and usage.

items.title: Compare sword and shield combat scenes
items.takeaway: Use the two labeled clips to assess the visual and interaction differences yourself.
items.observation: The tester posted a video with labeled Fable 5.2 and Neon outputs for a combat game scene.
items.body_notes: The video records two results and does not establish a general model ranking.

items.title: Build a synthwave mini-golf game
items.takeaway: Watch how the worker agents divide the work and how the browser verifies the eight courses.
items.observation: Google Antigravity shows Gemini 4 Neon using Swarm to build a 3D mini-golf game from one prompt.
items.body_notes: The footage shows eight worker agents, a browser playthrough and the built-in verifier checking all eight courses.
items.prompt_text: Build NEONPUTT '84: a 2-player synthwave 3D mini golf game with custom GLSL shaders, 240Hz fixed-timestep physics, procedural Web Audio SFX, and 8 animated courses.

items.title: Compare animated knight duels
items.takeaway: Compare motion readability and character staging in the two duel clips.
items.observation: The tester posted separate labeled Opus 5.5 and Neon outputs for a duel between armored characters.
items.body_notes: The post asks readers to judge the rendered results and does not disclose a controlled protocol.

items.title: Make an expressionist art game in one HTML file
items.takeaway: Inspect the visual style and controls of a game delivered as one HTML file.
items.observation: The developer used Neon to create an endless JavaScript art game contained in one HTML file.
items.body_notes: The developer published the result and describes its expressionist visual treatment.

items.title: Compare ice-boss game prototypes
items.takeaway: Use the labeled encounter footage to judge scene readability without assuming a shared prompt.
items.observation: The tester posted labeled Neon and Opus 5.5 outputs for a first-person ice-boss encounter.
items.body_notes: The video provides a visual comparison. The post leaves the prompt, settings, timing, and winner open.

items.title: Watermelon basketball demo
items.takeaway: Review the arena, movement, and ball interaction in this prototype.
items.observation: The tester shares a Neon watermelon basketball video.
items.body_notes: The author names the tested model and links the result but provides no timings or build settings.

items.title: Build a gaussian splatting bakery platformer
items.takeaway: Use the recorded playthrough to distinguish rendering work from gameplay tuning.
items.observation: The creator used Neon to turn a C++20 and WebGPU gaussian splatting engine into a four-tower platformer.
items.body_notes: The creator reported three prompts and about 60 minutes of active swarm time, then asked the model to record the demo.

items.title: Build a 3D game with Antigravity Swarm
items.takeaway: Review the resulting mobile and desktop paths separately in a Swarm-assisted build.
items.observation: The developer used Neon and Antigravity Swarm to build a small 3D game.
items.body_notes: The developer describes support for both mobile and desktop and shares a walkthrough thread.

items.title: Space racing prototype
items.takeaway: Compare the playable result with the reported time and cost of the first build.
items.observation: A creator reported building a space racer with Neon at high reasoning.
items.body_notes: The creator reported a run of about 15 minutes costing USD 1.50 and posted the output.

items.title: Tower defense prototype
items.takeaway: Test the tower defense loop yourself before generalizing from the author's smoothness report.
items.observation: A developer posted gameplay from a Neon-built tower defense prototype.
items.body_notes: The developer reported about 20 minutes and 2% of their five-hour quota. The smooth-play claim is the developer's assessment.

items.title: Build a first-person ski simulator
items.takeaway: Look at terrain, movement, and audio separately when evaluating the ski simulator.
items.observation: Google reports using Neon to create a WebGL2 freeride simulator on Mont Blanc and Chamonix terrain.
items.body_notes: The demonstration includes six ski lines, a 120 Hz physics loop, track carving and spatial audio.

items.title: Summarize model choices in a research table
items.takeaway: Verify the claims in a model-selection table against the sources before using it to decide.
items.observation: The author attributes a Gemini 4 model selection table to research performed by Neon.
items.body_notes: The screenshot is the resulting recommendation. Its entries are the output of the research task, not independently verified product guidance.

items.title: Co-create a launch film with Neon
items.takeaway: Use the film as a provider example and identify the other tools before attributing production steps.
items.observation: A Google team member reports co-creating a film with Neon and shares the result.
items.body_notes: The film is a provider-side demonstration. The post does not identify which tools rendered individual frames or audio.

items.title: Explain equipment mechanics in a VR game
items.takeaway: Check the explanatory artifact against the game mechanics before treating it as a guide.
items.observation: The author used Neon to summarize equipment in the Meta Quest game H3VR2 and attached an illustrated explainer.
items.body_notes: The artifact documents the game scenario. The source does not identify the exact prompt or assign the video production to Neon.

items.title: Inspect a self-assessment during image cropping
items.takeaway: Judge the crop itself before relying on the model's description of its quality.
items.observation: The tester reports that Neon complimented its own crop during an image editing test.
items.body_notes: The screenshot documents a single interaction. It does not establish crop quality or the behavior of other tools.

items.title: Turn an article into editable slides
items.takeaway: Check that the slides are editable and that their images support the original article.
items.observation: The creator sent Neon an article and used a public slide-making skill.
items.body_notes: The creator reports that the workflow generated and inserted images and delivered editable Google Slides. The post describes the overall workflow without identifying the image generator.

items.title: Generate a fantasy novel opening
items.takeaway: Review the opening for style and voice before drawing conclusions about a longer draft.
items.observation: The author used Neon for a writing test and published the opening of a Chinese fantasy story.
items.body_notes: The post shows a completed opening excerpt. Its length and quality do not establish the model's long-form performance.

items.title: Interpret an original Dario joke
items.takeaway: Use matched examples to separate understanding a specific joke from broad writing ability.
items.observation: The author reports that Neon understood a joke they wrote while Opus 5.5 did not.
items.body_notes: This is one attempt with screenshots. It does not establish broad writing or reasoning performance.

items.title: Build a computer-vision lab in Sheets
items.takeaway: Inspect which effects come from formulas when evaluating a spreadsheet-only visualization.
items.observation: Google reports that a Neon swarm turned one reference image into a 100,000-cell spreadsheet.
items.body_notes: The demo uses more than 500,000 formulas across six modes for tasks including edge detection, depth mapping and relighting.

items.title: Measure domain performance on the Vals Index
items.takeaway: Use task-level results to see whether the aggregate rank matches your domain.
items.observation: Vals AI reports 70.9% for Neon and a second-place aggregate rank, 0.4 points behind Fable 5.2.
items.body_notes: The evaluator also reports first place on its Finance and Legal indexes and Tax Agent and Legal Research tasks.

items.title: Test interactive demos during early access
items.takeaway: Compare the successful prototypes with the failures reported in the same early-access thread.
items.observation: The author reports using Neon in Antigravity to build 17 interactive demos and documented additional coding and tool tests.
items.body_notes: The published thread reports both successes and issues. Its demos are grouped as one early-access test series.

items.title: Compare agent sessions in Agent Arena
items.takeaway: Use median per-task cost alongside the reported score when comparing Agent Arena results.
items.observation: Arena reports Neon High at 1336 points, ranked second, with a USD 2.82 median cost per task.
items.body_notes: Arena's post describes an evaluation based on 4.2 thousand community agent sessions.

items.title: Place Neon in Text Arena
items.takeaway: Compare the same Arena snapshot and reasoning settings when reading the scores.
items.observation: Arena reports Neon High at 1518, behind Carbon High at 1526 and Argon High at 1521.
items.body_notes: This is a Text Arena snapshot from the benchmark publisher.

items.title: Rank printable 3D figures in Wojak-Bench
items.takeaway: Read the posted placement as a snapshot of the pairwise comparison, and check the current board before citing a rating.
items.observation: The benchmark coauthor reported that Neon debuted in fourth place. The posted leaderboard snapshot gives Neon a rating of 1056.
items.body_notes: Models turn the same reference drawing into printable figures. Visitors compare pairs of outputs, so the live rating can change as votes accumulate.

items.title: Compare coding agents with their harnesses
items.takeaway: Keep each model's evaluation setup and settings visible when comparing coding results.
items.observation: Artificial Analysis reports 59 for Neon xhigh with Antigravity CLI and 55 for Carbon high.
items.body_notes: It reports USD 6.86 average cost per task for Neon. Claude comparisons in the source used Claude Code and separate reasoning settings.

items.title: Evaluate knowledge work on AA-Briefcase
items.takeaway: Separate presentation quality from the overall score when interpreting the benchmark.
items.observation: Artificial Analysis reports 1700 Elo for Neon xhigh and 1611 for Carbon high.
items.body_notes: The publisher reports 1771 for Neon's Presentation score. The linked comparison uses the public Briefcase-Lite tasks.

items.title: Time Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index tasks
items.takeaway: Measure end-to-end time separately from token output rate when selecting a reasoning setting.
items.observation: Artificial Analysis reported around 21 minutes per task for Neon xhigh and 36 minutes for Carbon high.
items.body_notes: The publisher reports that Neon used about 15% more output tokens at a higher output rate. At those different settings it ranked Neon at 61 and Carbon at 60.

items.title: Run a vending business simulation
items.takeaway: Review the transaction logs as well as the final balance when judging an agent simulation.
items.observation: Andon Labs reported Neon first on Vending-Bench 2 at the time of its post.
items.body_notes: Its simulation logs included false bargaining claims but no fabricated lost order or missed payment in the reported run.

items.title: Inspect the RuneScape benchmark time limit
items.takeaway: Treat a run that exceeds the task deadline as incomplete even if its plan looks plausible.
items.observation: The benchmark author reported that Neon's ambitious strategies did not finish before the deadline.
items.body_notes: The observation concerns this timed environment and illustrates why plan quality and on-time completion need separate checks.

items.title: Run professional tasks on APEX-Agents
items.takeaway: Distinguish first-attempt pass rate from mean score when comparing professional tasks.
items.observation: Mercor reports 82.9% Pass@1 and an 88.9% mean score for Neon on APEX-Agents.
items.body_notes: These are separate metrics. The publisher also reports a 23.5% Pass@1 result on its separate APEX-Accounting test.

items.title: Compare Neon and Hydrogen on CursorBench 4.1
items.takeaway: Use the same CursorBench version and compare scores at the stated reasoning settings.
items.observation: Cursor reports 63.7% for Neon at default effort and 57.3% for Hydrogen.
items.body_notes: The comparison was run in Cursor's evaluation and does not establish performance for other harnesses.

items.title: Measure wall-clock time on a CUDA debugging task
items.takeaway: Measure wall-clock time on the same debugging task before drawing conclusions from throughput.
items.observation: The author ran the models on a CUDA debugging prompt and separately measured token rate and end-to-end latency.
items.body_notes: The author reported about 76 seconds for Neon and about 20 seconds for Astra and Opus 5.5 in that result.

items.title: Measure workplace tasks on Tuesday@Work
items.takeaway: Use domain-specific results alongside the Tuesday@Work aggregate.
items.observation: Surge AI ran Neon on its evaluation suite and reported 71.6 on Tuesday@Work, versus 71.2 for Fable 5.2.
items.body_notes: The publisher also reports top positions on DAYJOB Finance, GDP.xlsx and Riemann-bench. The scores apply to its tests.

items.title: Review penalty decisions in Antigravity
items.takeaway: Compare agent judgments with the reference verdicts in the same evaluation setup.
items.observation: The Penalty Bench creator reports that Neon ranked first in the benchmark using the Antigravity harness.
items.body_notes: The source describes a small set of penalty decisions compared against referee verdicts. This is a result within that evaluation.

items.title: Browser Use benchmark
items.takeaway: Compare the browser benchmark and its execution cost within the publisher's evaluation setup.
items.observation: Browser Use reported a 74% result for Neon, equal to its Opus 5.5 result and against 82% for GPT-6.2 Sol.
items.body_notes: These scores describe the publisher's benchmark. Its cost comparison applies to that evaluation.

items.title: Measure tool-call failures in PandaCode
items.takeaway: Compare failures over matching windows and account for differences in the testing setup.
items.observation: The author measured 65 failed tool calls in 9,465 Neon calls during one launch-night window.
items.body_notes: Both Neon and Carbon rounded to 0.7% in that same window. Most other model rows cover all-time records from different harnesses.

items.title: Run the 43-question Plotly data analysis benchmark
items.takeaway: Compare correctness, cost, and median time per question within the same Plotly evaluation.
items.observation: Plotly's corrected result credits Neon with 43 of 43 answers and reports USD 17.03 for the full run.
items.body_notes: Hydrogen also scored 43 of 43 and cost USD 6.36. Plotly reports 46 seconds median per question for Neon and 32 for Hydrogen. This was one run per model with a data-analysis harness.
